title: A job declares its permissions and its secrets; nothing is passed undeclared
A job declares the secrets it receives; nothing is passed undeclared
body:
Part of epic gcd-cf98 (unit 1 of plan git-dev-aef7, record mangimangi/git-dev .pearls/docs/epics/git-dev-aef7.md; delivers into plan/git-dev-aef7). Planning doc: .pearls/docs/epics/gcd-cf98.md.

## Problem
Which secret a job's scripts get is decided by the trigger, not the job. On merge, cron and manual the run job passes VENDOR_PAT (templates/workflows/merge.yml line 179, cron.yml line 157, manual.yml line 195: 'VENDOR_PAT: ${{ secrets.VENDOR_PAT }}' in the env of the 'Run job' step of the 'run' matrix job); on open it is withheld (OPEN_WITHHELD_ENV = frozenset({'VENDOR_PAT'}) at git-cicd line 973, applied in script_env() at line 976, whose docstring around line 983 states the rule; run_job() at line 1023 builds the env via script_env). So this repository's release job receives VENDOR_PAT though it never uses it, and a pull-request job cannot read a private repository (pearls'/madreperla's toolchain-contract check needs a read token) nor write (git-semver's version check will push a bump to the PR branch, unit 2 of the plan).

## Decided (do not reopen)
- Two tokens named for what they can do: CICD_WRITE_TOKEN replaces VENDOR_PAT (pushes branches, opens pull requests, writes workflow files); CICD_READ_TOKEN is new (reads private repositories, cannot write). VENDOR_PAT stays declarable, documented as deprecated, so a repo can upgrade before renaming its secret.
- Nothing is passed undeclared, on any trigger, from this release (breaking).
- GITHUB_TOKEN is still given to every job unchanged; an open job that declares nothing gets exactly what it gets today.
- Injection rules hold: a declared name is a validated identifier; no value from the config reaches a run: block; a secret reaches a script only as an environment variable.
- No existing row or status name changes.

## Scope
1. Config field. Add 'secrets' to JOB_FIELDS (git-cicd line 59) and validate it in _validate_job() (git-cicd lines 360-501): an array of distinct strings, each one of the documented set CICD_WRITE_TOKEN, CICD_READ_TOKEN, VENDOR_PAT (a module constant, e.g. DECLARABLE_SECRETS, replacing OPEN_WITHHELD_ENV). validate refuses: a non-array or a non-string entry (malformed), a name outside the set, and a duplicate; each message starts 'job <name>:' and says the reason (for an unknown name, list the allowed names). The normalized job carries 'secrets' (list, default []). Document the field in templates/config.schema (the jobs description and a property for secrets with the enum), saying VENDOR_PAT is deprecated.
2. Script environment. script_env() (line 976) removes every name of the documented set from the inherited environment unless the job declares it, on every trigger (open, merge, cron, manual, and so a local check). A declared secret that is empty or unset in the caller's environment is removed too, so it reaches the script as unset, never as an empty string. Rewrite the docstring to state the new rule. GITHUB_TOKEN keeps passing through unchanged. git-cicd never prints a secret value.
3. Report absent secrets. The run-job result record (built in run_job, line 1023) gains a field listing the declared secrets that were absent (names only); the report (job_rows / format_report / format_markdown) shows them by name on that job's row or as a note under it, e.g. 'declared secret CICD_WRITE_TOKEN is not set'. run-job also prints the same note before the steps. A job whose results lack the field (older result files) reports as today. No value is ever printed in log, report or error.
4. Workflows. In templates/workflows/merge.yml, cron.yml, manual.yml replace the 'VENDOR_PAT: ${{ secrets.VENDOR_PAT }}' line, and in open.yml add, so that the 'Run job' step gives a matrix job only the secrets its config job declares. Decision (recorded): select per matrix entry with an expression over a new decide output, e.g. decide's GitHub output (write_github_output, git-cicd line 938) gains 'secrets' = JSON {job: [declared names]}, and the step env has one line per documented name of the form 'CICD_WRITE_TOKEN: ${{ contains(fromJSON(needs.decide.outputs.secrets)[matrix.job], 'CICD_WRITE_TOKEN') && secrets.CICD_WRITE_TOKEN || '' }}' (and likewise for CICD_READ_TOKEN and VENDOR_PAT). Reason: the secret names are a fixed documented set, so the templates stay fixed text (no generate/verify change needed for secrets) and no config value reaches the workflow; an undeclared secret's value is never given to the runner step at all, and the empty string an undeclared/unset name gets is removed by script_env (item 2), so the script sees no secret, not an empty one. The implementer must confirm against GitHub's documentation (contexts and expressions: secrets context, the && || ternary idiom, fromJSON over job outputs) that this works and that the empty-string fallback never exposes a value; if the docs show it does not work, choose another mechanism that keeps the templates free of config values and record the change in the issue. Update the header comments of each template that describe secrets/permissions (merge.yml lines ~29-35, cron.yml ~33, manual.yml ~45, open.yml ~6). Regenerate .github/workflows/git-cicd-*.yml with ./git-cicd generate and commit them (this repo's config declares nothing yet; its own declarations are issue 3 of this epic).
5. Remove the trigger rule: VENDOR_PAT is passed to no job that does not declare it; OPEN_WITHHELD_ENV and its uses go.

## Tests (pytest under tests/, following existing patterns)
- tests/test_config.py: validate refuses an unknown secret name, a non-array value, a non-string entry, and a duplicate, each with a message naming the job; accepts each documented name; normalized default is [].
- tests/test_run.py (run-job, run through Repo.run like the existing tests): on each trigger (open, merge, cron, manual), with CICD_WRITE_TOKEN, CICD_READ_TOKEN and VENDOR_PAT all set in the caller's environment, a job that declares nothing sees none of them; a job that declares CICD_READ_TOKEN sees it and nothing else; a declared secret set to empty or unset reaches the script as unset and the result/report names it as absent; GITHUB_TOKEN still reaches every job. Replace tests/test_check.py lines 183-189 (the VENDOR_PAT-on-open check test) with the new rule through check.
- tests/test_workflow.py: replace the assertions at lines 91-98 and 123-125 (VENDOR_PAT absent from open.yml, present on the others) with: every run job's step env carries exactly the selection lines for the documented set, no template contains 'secrets.' outside them, and no config value appears in the env.
- tests/test_report.py: the absent-secrets note appears by name, and a test asserts a secret value set in the environment never appears in run-job output, the result file or the report.
- Token guard: every test runs with CICD_WRITE_TOKEN, CICD_READ_TOKEN, VENDOR_PAT, GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN removed from the environment: an autouse fixture in tests/conftest.py (next to the existing GITHUB_/CICD_ removal in the repo fixture, line ~105) deletes them for every test, and tests/bats/helper.bash (which already unsets GH_TOKEN CI at line 20) unsets all five in setup. A test fails if that guard is removed: decision (recorded) — ci/test.sh exports sentinel values for the five names before running pytest and bats, and a pytest test and a bats test each assert none of the five is in the environment, so removing the guard makes them fail whenever the suite runs through ci/test.sh (as check and CI run it). Add a bats test of ci/test.sh's exports if needed to keep shell coverage. Tests that need a token (e.g. tests/test_own_jobs.py lines 139-274, tests/bats/update-vendored.bats) set fake values explicitly.
- Coverage of git-cicd stays at or above 99% (pyproject.toml fail_under).

## Acceptance criteria
- An open job that declares CICD_READ_TOKEN receives it and nothing else; one that declares nothing receives no secret even when the caller's environment has all three; shown by run-job tests.
- On every trigger, including a local check, a script's environment holds a documented secret if and only if its job declares it and it is set non-empty.
- The generated workflows give each job only the secrets it declares; no job that does not declare VENDOR_PAT gets it.
- The report names absent declared secrets by name only; no secret value appears in any log, report or error.
- validate refuses an unknown secret name, a malformed declaration and a duplicate, each naming the job.
- The token guard exists in pytest and bats and a test fails when it is removed.
- ./git-cicd check passes with coverage >= 99%; ./git-cicd verify passes after generate.
- No vendor-protected file is added, changed or deleted (python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-aef7 reports nothing).

## Out of scope
Permissions declarations (separate issue in this epic); this repository's own job declarations, README rule rewrite, CHANGELOG and VERSION bump (issue 3 of this epic); any change in git-semver or git-vendored; secrets outside the documented set; a GitHub App identity.

title: A job declares the permissions its workflow token needs
body:
Part of epic gcd-cf98 (unit 1 of plan git-dev-aef7, record mangimangi/git-dev .pearls/docs/epics/git-dev-aef7.md; delivers into plan/git-dev-aef7). Planning doc: .pearls/docs/epics/gcd-cf98.md. Depends on gcd-cf98.1 (secrets declarations; same validation code, templates and decide outputs — do it after to avoid conflicts).

## Problem
The token permissions of the job that runs a repository's scripts are fixed by trigger: the 'run' matrix job gets 'contents: write' and 'pull-requests: write' on merge, cron and manual (templates/workflows/merge.yml lines 156-157, cron.yml lines 134-135, manual.yml lines 172-173) and the top-level 'contents: read' on open (open.yml line 67; its run job at ~line 133 sets no permissions). A job cannot publish packages: medici's image workflows push to the container registry and need 'packages: write'; they cannot stay a separate workflow chained off the release (a tag or release made with a workflow's own token starts no workflow), so it must be a later step of the release job, which cannot get the permission. 'packages: write' is a permission of the workflow's own token (GITHUB_TOKEN); no personal token is involved.

## Platform constraint (verify against GitHub's documentation; do not assume)
All config jobs on one trigger run as entries of one 'run' matrix job, and a GitHub job's 'permissions' applies to every matrix entry. The implementer must look up whether job-level 'permissions' accepts expressions (it is expected not to: values are literal read/write/none), and record the finding in this issue. Decision (recorded): because permissions cannot vary per matrix entry at run time, generate writes, per trigger, one extra run job per distinct effective permission set that differs from the trigger's default (e.g. job ids run-1, run-2 in first-seen config order, or an id derived from the set), each with the trigger default plus that set written literally, and a matrix from a new decide output listing that group's needed entries (the open/merge/manual 'jobs' list; on cron the (job, branch) 'runs' list, see write_github_output git-cicd line 938). The default 'run' job's matrix excludes those jobs. Reason: it is the only way, given literal permissions, that two jobs on the same trigger run with different permissions, and it keeps the template structure for repos that declare nothing byte-identical to today. Rows: each group job's matrix entries show the same row name as today (<title> / <repo>:<job>); no existing row or status name changes. A group job that has nothing to run must not show a raw '${{ ... }}' name: the README (Rows section, lines ~318-355) explains that a matrix job skipped before its matrix is evaluated shows its raw name, which is why 'run' uses the '(nothing)' placeholder (NOTHING_JOB, git-cicd line ~66). The implementer checks how a skipped group job renders and either skips it with a job-level if that renders cleanly or gives it a placeholder entry with a distinct documented title; record the choice here and document any new row in README's Rows table. The report job's 'needs:' includes every group job; the per-job result artifact names (git-cicd-result-<job>) are unchanged so job_rows/report keep working. The group jobs carry the same concurrency, checkout and step env (including gcd-cf98.1's secret selection) as 'run'.

## Scope
1. Config field 'permissions' (add to JOB_FIELDS, git-cicd line 59; validate in _validate_job, lines 360-501): an object mapping a scope to a level, mirroring GitHub's syntax, e.g. {"packages": "write"}. Decision (recorded): the documented set of scopes is contents, pull-requests, issues, packages; levels read and write. Reason: covers the epic's needs (packages: write) and the scopes the triggers already use, kept small so each is documented. validate refuses, each with a message starting 'job <name>:' and the reason: a non-object value or non-string level (malformed), a scope outside the set (listing the allowed scopes), a level other than read/write, and any write level on a job whose 'on' contains open. Decision (recorded): no write permission is allowed on open; reason: open runs a pull request's own code (GitHub already forces a read-only token for fork pull requests), and the one open job that must write (git-semver's version check pushing a bump, unit 2) does so with a declared CICD_WRITE_TOKEN secret (gcd-cf98.1), not the workflow token; the schema and README say why. Effective permissions on a trigger = the trigger's default merged with the declaration, the higher level winning (defaults: open contents: read; merge, cron, manual contents: write and pull-requests: write); a declaration that adds nothing beyond the default is accepted and leaves the job in the default 'run' job. A job that declares none keeps its trigger's default. Document the field in templates/config.schema (jobs description and a property with the enums).
2. decide: the decision/GitHub outputs carry, per group, the needed entries; existing outputs (jobs, names, any, max_parallel, runs) keep their meaning for the default 'run' job.
3. generate (render_workflow line 1178, render_workflows line 1224, alongside schedule_block line 1124 and form_block line 1142): the templates gain a placeholder (like __SCHEDULE__ / __FORM__) where group jobs are written; group jobs are rendered deterministically, permission values written from the validated set only (no free config text in the file beyond validated identifiers). Update template header comments describing permissions (merge.yml ~29-35, cron.yml ~33, manual.yml ~45, open.yml ~6) and the 'Every generated file is fixed text except ...' sentences. render with this repository's config (no declarations) is byte-identical to the committed .github/workflows/git-cicd-*.yml.
4. verify (verify_workflow line 1244) fails when the generated files and the declarations disagree (it already compares whole files; add tests proving it for a declaration added, changed and removed) and passes after generate.

## Tests (pytest, following tests/test_config.py, tests/test_decide.py, tests/test_workflow.py patterns)
- validate: refuses an unknown scope, an unknown level, a malformed value (non-object, non-string level), and a write level on a job with open in on; each message names the job.
- generate: with two jobs on merge, one declaring packages: write and one declaring nothing, the generated merge workflow has a job whose permissions are contents: write, pull-requests: write, packages: write and whose matrix comes from that group's output, and the default run job keeps contents: write, pull-requests: write without packages; the sibling is in the default job only. Same for cron (runs matrix) and manual. Two jobs with the same effective set share one group job.
- decide outputs list each job in exactly one group.
- verify fails after a declaration is added or changed without regenerating, and passes after generate.
- Coverage of git-cicd stays >= 99%.

## Acceptance criteria
- A job that declares packages: write runs with it and a sibling job on the same trigger does not; shown on the generated workflow.
- A job that declares nothing keeps its trigger's default; a config with no declarations generates exactly today's files.
- validate refuses an unknown permission, a disallowed level, a malformed declaration and a write on open, each naming the job.
- ./git-cicd verify fails after a declaration is added or changed without regenerating, and passes after generate.
- No existing row or status name changes; any new row is documented.
- ./git-cicd check passes with coverage >= 99%; python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-aef7 reports nothing.

## Out of scope
This repository's own declarations, README rewrite, CHANGELOG and VERSION (gcd-cf98.3); secrets (gcd-cf98.1); permissions outside the documented set; an image or runtime per job; any change in git-semver or git-vendored.

title: git-cicd's own jobs declare what they need; README states the rule; minor version bump
body:
Part of epic gcd-cf98 (unit 1 of plan git-dev-aef7, record mangimangi/git-dev .pearls/docs/epics/git-dev-aef7.md; delivers into plan/git-dev-aef7). Planning doc: .pearls/docs/epics/gcd-cf98.md. Depends on gcd-cf98.1 (job 'secrets' declaration) and gcd-cf98.2 (job 'permissions' declaration); do it last.

## Scope
1. .vendored/configs/git-cicd.json (editable; not vendor-protected): update-vendored declares "secrets": ["CICD_WRITE_TOKEN", "VENDOR_PAT"] (VENDOR_PAT kept so it keeps working until the owner renames the secret); release, test, vendor-check and version-check declare nothing (no secrets, no permissions) — today release receives VENDOR_PAT though it never uses it, and after this it does not. Update the update-vendored 'private' input description, now 'Vendor repo is private (use VENDOR_PAT)', to name the new token (e.g. 'use CICD_WRITE_TOKEN'), and its mirror in tests/test_own_jobs.py line ~81.
2. ci/update-vendored.sh: today 'export GH_TOKEN="${VENDOR_PAT:-${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}}"' (line 12). Change to use the first that is set of CICD_WRITE_TOKEN, VENDOR_PAT, then GITHUB_TOKEN; update its header comment (lines 1-9). Extend tests/bats/update-vendored.bats (existing tests at lines 37-44: 'GH_TOKEN is VENDOR_PAT when set', 'GH_TOKEN is GITHUB_TOKEN without VENDOR_PAT') with: CICD_WRITE_TOKEN wins over VENDOR_PAT; VENDOR_PAT used without CICD_WRITE_TOKEN; GITHUB_TOKEN without either. Update tests/test_own_jobs.py (lines ~139-274, the update-vendored run_job tests passing VENDOR_PAT) accordingly.
3. Regenerate and commit .github/workflows/git-cicd-*.yml (./git-cicd generate; the Manual form changes with the input description). ./git-cicd verify passes.
4. Tests on this repository's config (tests/test_own_jobs.py patterns): with CICD_WRITE_TOKEN, CICD_READ_TOKEN and VENDOR_PAT all set in the caller's environment, run-job of update-vendored sees CICD_WRITE_TOKEN and VENDOR_PAT (not CICD_READ_TOKEN) and run-job of release sees none of the three, on merge, cron and manual runs as each job's triggers allow (release: merge and manual; update-vendored: cron and manual); and the generated workflows (rendered from the own config) give update-vendored's matrix entry only those two secrets and release none.
5. README.md:
   - 'The config' / 'A job declares' (line ~61): document the 'secrets' and 'permissions' fields (documented sets, levels, refusals, write not allowed on open and why, VENDOR_PAT deprecated).
   - 'What a script is given' (line ~257): replace the trigger/secret table (lines ~273-292, '| Trigger | GITHUB_TOKEN | VENDOR_PAT |' and the paragraphs on VENDOR_PAT and on an open job that read a private vendor) with the rule: a job gets what it declares; GITHUB_TOKEN to every job; an undeclared secret is removed from the caller's environment on every trigger including check; a declared secret not set reaches the script unset and the report names it.
   - Give an example for each of the three needs: a release job that publishes packages (permissions {"packages": "write"}); a pull request job that reads a private repository with CICD_READ_TOKEN; a job that proposes changes with CICD_WRITE_TOKEN.
   - Say what each token is for and what permissions a fine-grained personal access token needs for it: CICD_READ_TOKEN — Contents: read (and Metadata: read) on the private repositories it reads; CICD_WRITE_TOKEN — Contents: read and write, Pull requests: read and write, Workflows: read and write (to write workflow files), on the repositories it changes. Verify these names against GitHub's fine-grained token documentation.
   - 'The generated workflows' (line ~459, including the VENDOR_PAT mention at ~501): describe the run job's permissions per trigger, the per-permission-set run jobs from gcd-cf98.2 and that generate/verify cover them, and how a step's env selects declared secrets (gcd-cf98.1). Update the Rows table if gcd-cf98.2 added a row.
   - 'Running the checks locally' (line ~812, VENDOR_PAT removed on open): state the new rule for check.
   - 'Not built yet' (line ~836): replace 'Secrets beyond GITHUB_TOKEN and VENDOR_PAT (which open does not get)' with secrets outside the documented set and a GitHub App identity; keep 'An image or runtime per job'.
   - 'Developing git-cicd' (own jobs table line ~852): update-vendored's GH_TOKEN is CICD_WRITE_TOKEN when set, else VENDOR_PAT, else GITHUB_TOKEN; note what each own job declares.
   - Upgrade steps for an adopter, in order: (1) declare secrets/permissions on each job that needs them (a job that used VENDOR_PAT declares it, or CICD_WRITE_TOKEN / CICD_READ_TOKEN); (2) add the renamed secret(s) CICD_WRITE_TOKEN / CICD_READ_TOKEN in the repository settings; (3) run generate; (4) commit the config and generated workflows. Place it in 'Installing' (line ~692) next to the upgrade text, or a migration subsection like 'Migrating from the single git-cicd.yml' (line ~680).
6. AGENTS.md: where it describes the jobs/update-vendored, say that update-vendored declares CICD_WRITE_TOKEN and VENDOR_PAT and the others declare nothing (keep everything else).
7. Version: run .vendored/pkg/git-semver/git-semver bump minor --no-push --description "..." (0.1.0 -> 0.2.0), which updates VERSION and CHANGELOG.md and commits them. The changelog entry marks the release breaking and says what breaks for whom: a job on merge, cron or manual that used VENDOR_PAT without declaring it no longer receives it (declare it, or rename to CICD_WRITE_TOKEN and declare that; run generate and commit); an inherited secret of the documented set is removed from every undeclared job's environment, including locally; new: declared secrets CICD_READ_TOKEN/CICD_WRITE_TOKEN and declared permissions. Reference the issue IDs gcd-cf98.1, gcd-cf98.2, gcd-cf98.3 as the 0.1.0 entries do.

## Acceptance criteria
- With this repository's config, the update-vendored job's script sees CICD_WRITE_TOKEN (and VENDOR_PAT) and the release job's script sees neither, on merge, cron and manual runs; shown by tests on run-job and on the generated files.
- ci/update-vendored.sh uses CICD_WRITE_TOKEN, else VENDOR_PAT, else GITHUB_TOKEN; bats tests show each.
- The generated workflows are regenerated and committed; ./git-cicd verify passes.
- README replaces the trigger/secret table with the rule, documents both declarations with the three examples, the tokens' purposes and fine-grained permissions, and the ordered upgrade steps; 'Not built yet' updated.
- VERSION is 0.2.0 and CHANGELOG.md has a breaking entry; .vendored/pkg/git-semver/git-semver check-bump passes against origin/main.
- ./git-cicd check passes with coverage >= 99%.
- The pull request into plan/git-dev-aef7 has a passing Verdict / git-cicd:verdict.
- python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-aef7 reports nothing (no vendor-protected file added, changed or deleted).

## Out of scope
Renaming the repository secret itself (the owner does that in settings); any change in git-semver or git-vendored (units 2 and 3); pushing a version bump from CI; migrating a consumer (pearls, madreperla, medici).
